chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr from al-Qasim ibn Sulayman from 'Ubayd ibn Zur'arah from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding a man who gave charity on behalf of his children who have reached maturity, he said: 'If they do not take possession (of it) until he dies, then it is inheritance. And if he gives charity on behalf of those who have not reached maturity from among his children, then it is valid, because the father is the one who manages their affairs.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a father giving charity on behalf of his minor versus adult children?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the distinction between a father's management of his minor children's property versus their independent ownership upon maturity. The hadith establishes that for mature children, the father's gift remains revocable until actual possession (qabd), whereas for minors, the father's authority allows for immediate validity, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of the father as the natural guardian (wali) of his underage offspring's assets.
